classification.difficultyReason: Model savings as a percentage of hourly earnings and solve a minimum-value inequality.

content.prompt: Suppose that you work for $\$25.50$ per hour. Of the total you earn, you save 25%. How many hours must you work in a week to save at least $\$163$?

answer.short:
At least $\dfrac{1304}{51}$ hours, approximately $25.57$ hours.

Save 25% of the hourly earnings and solve the resulting inequality.
answer.worked:
Let $h$ be the number of hours worked in a week.
$$\begin{align*}0.25\times25.50h&\ge163\\6.375h&\ge163\\h&\ge\frac{163}{6.375}\\h&\ge\frac{1304}{51}\end{align*}$$
The minimum is $\dfrac{1304}{51}=25.568627\ldots$ hours, approximately $25.57$ hours. Working $25.57$ hours saves $\$163.00875$, which meets the target.
